settings.label: Directory (tenant) ID
settings.meaning: The tenant whose users sign in and whose directory the app manages. For an app that accepts any work or school tenant, `organizations` (or `common`, which adds personal Microsoft accounts); Graph user calls then need the app's own tenant instead.
settings.whereToFind: Microsoft Entra admin center › App registrations › your app › Overview › Directory (tenant) ID. Entra has no test mode: use a separate tenant for test.

settings.label: Application (client) ID
settings.meaning: The app registration: the audience of the access tokens the app accepts, and the client that signs users in and calls Microsoft Graph.
settings.whereToFind: Microsoft Entra admin center › App registrations › your app › Overview › Application (client) ID. A separate registration in the test tenant.

settings.label: Client secret
settings.meaning: Proves the app to Entra when it redeems a sign-in code, refreshes tokens and calls Microsoft Graph. Not needed by an app that only checks tokens.
settings.whereToFind: Microsoft Entra admin center › App registrations › your app › Certificates & secrets › Client secrets › New client secret: copy the Value (not the Secret ID) when it's shown. Graph user calls need application permissions (User.ReadWrite.All) granted admin consent under API permissions.

settings.label: Sign-in address
settings.meaning: Only for a Microsoft Entra External ID (customer) tenant: the tenant's own sign-in host, https://<subdomain>.ciamlogin.com. Leave it unset for a workforce tenant (https://login.microsoftonline.com).
settings.whereToFind: https://<subdomain>.ciamlogin.com, where <subdomain> is the part of the tenant's primary domain before .onmicrosoft.com (Microsoft Entra admin center › Overview › Primary domain).

settings.label: Change notification secret
settings.meaning: The clientState the app gives Microsoft Graph when it subscribes to user changes; every notification carries it back, which is how the app knows Graph sent it.
settings.whereToFind: A random string of your own, at most 128 characters: the subscription helper sends it to Graph.

operations.name: discovery.get
operations.purpose: Reads the tenant's OpenID configuration, GET {authority}/{tenant}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration: its issuer and where its signing keys are.

operations.name: keys.list
operations.purpose: Reads the tenant's signing keys from the jwks_uri the OpenID configuration names.

operations.name: tokens.exchangeCode
operations.purpose: Redeems an authorization code and its PKCE verifier for tokens, POST {authority}/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token with grant_type=authorization_code.

operations.name: tokens.refresh
operations.purpose: Exchanges a refresh token for new tokens, POST {authority}/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token with grant_type=refresh_token. Entra may return a new refresh token; the old one is then discarded.

operations.name: tokens.appToken
operations.purpose: Gets the app's own token for Microsoft Graph, POST {authority}/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token with grant_type=client_credentials and scope https://graph.microsoft.com/.default.

operations.name: users.get
operations.purpose: Reads one user of the directory by object id.

operations.name: users.find
operations.purpose: Finds users by mail or userPrincipalName with $filter (by their email sign-in identity in an External ID tenant).

operations.name: users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user: a member with a userPrincipalName in a workforce tenant, or a customer with an email sign-in identity in an External ID tenant.

operations.name: users.delete
operations.purpose: Deletes a user (Entra keeps it soft-deleted for 30 days).

operations.name: subscriptions.create
operations.purpose: Subscribes the app's webhook to changes of the directory's users, with the clientState every notification will carry.

operations.name: subscriptions.renew
operations.purpose: Moves a subscription's expiry later. Subscriptions on users last at most 41,760 minutes (under 29 days).

signature.description: Microsoft Graph signs nothing. The body is {"value": [notification, ...]} and each notification's clientState is the value the app gave when it subscribed: compare every one with it in constant time and refuse the delivery if any differs. Before a subscription is made, Graph checks the endpoint with a POST to the notification URL carrying ?validationToken=<token> and an empty body; answer 200 with Content-Type text/plain and the URL-decoded token as the body, within 10 seconds. Answer each delivery with a 2xx within 3 seconds (202 once it's queued), or Graph retries it for up to 4 hours.

events.meaning: A user was created, changed or soft-deleted: Graph sends all three as updated. The notification carries the user's id, not the user.
